market_view: Stocks ripped on Nov 4 after the Democratic midterm sweep (Dow +3.03% to 53,356, S&P 500 +1.58% to 7,688.62, Nasdaq +1.44%; TheStreet/StockTitan, Nov 4) as WTI fell ~8% and the 10-year eased to ~4.89%, with financials +3.1% and AI data-center names (CoreWeave -9.9%) the big losers; after a relief day this large I expect choppier follow-through, and tonight's after-hours movers (AppLovin +23%, Sezzle +33%, Qualcomm -7%) are already-priced gaps I won't buy at the open. Operator update updates/ALL.md only asks for evidence-backed lessons and dated research, which I followed; nothing was ignored.
lessons: I'm still losing to the market and both baselines: alpha -1.14% per trade over 82 trades (95% range -2.09% to -0.19%, p_beats_fly 0.041) versus -0.14% for the Fruit Fly and -0.72% for Momentum, and my moonshots (n=40, 15% win) and catalysts (n=43, 48.8% stopped) both lose. Tonight's best ideas are big after-hours gaps (APP +23%, SEZL +33%) and the lab shows +2% opening gaps lose 5.4% open-to-close (n=16, a hunch), so I again submit zero moonshots and zero catalysts.

My three non-AI compounders made +$9.25 on Nov 4 (BLK +5.4%, ABBV +3.1%, LLY +0.6%) and sit at +7.6%, +1.3% and +8.5%, while my AI-capex compounders stopped out (GOOGL -17.7%, NVDA -11.6%) and AI data-center names fell hard again today (CoreWeave -9.9%); compounder n=5 is a hunch, but I keep diversified, cash-generating holdings and add no AI-capex name.

ChatGPT has left two compounder slots empty for two nights rather than chase winners, and its alpha (+0.72%, n=28) beats mine; I'm keeping my two free slots empty too, because buying after a +1.6% S&P / +3.1% financials relief day means paying a gapped-up open, which the lab table shows is the worst entry. What I change: I raise stops on BLK and LLY to lock gains instead of adding risk.

review.reason: It jumped 5.4% to a new 52-week high of $1,224.37 (high $1,231.14) as the S&P 500 Financials index rose 3.1% on the post-election relief rally (rallies.ai, Nov 4), well above its $1,103.81 50-day (DailyPolitical, Nov 4); the Q3-inflection thesis is intact, and I raise the stop to $1,150 (~6.1% below, outside 1.5x its ~2% daily range) to lock a gain over the $1,136.26 entry.

Novo Nordisk raised 2026 guidance to -2% to +2% and its pill took ~80% of new Wegovy scripts (24/7 Wall St, Nov 4), but LLY still rose 0.61% to $1,417.99 inside a $1,401.59-$1,445.96 range, so the read-through didn't break the leader; I raise the stop to $1,360 (~4.1% below) to protect the +8.5% gain with the $1,460 target ~3% away.

It recovered 3.1% to $294.83 near its $294.89 record as health care rallied with hospitals and insurers after the election (StockTitan, Nov 4); the Oct 30 beat-and-raise thesis is intact and the $272 stop (~7.7% below) stays outside normal noise.
